memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "'Then I sent Moses and Aaron, and I afflicted the Egyptians by what I did there, and I brought you out. When I brought your people out of Egypt, you came to the sea, and the Egyptians pursued them with chariots and horsemen as far as the Red Sea. But they cried to the Lord for help, and he put darkness between you and the Egyptians; he brought the sea over them and covered them. You saw with your own eyes what I did to the Egyptians. Then you lived in the wilderness for a long time.'" — Josh 24:5-7 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
God continues His account, and the great rescue from Egypt comes into view. Once again the emphasis is on what God did: "I sent Moses," "I brought you out," "I did." When Israel was trapped at the Red Sea, helpless between the water and Pharaoh's army, they could do nothing but cry out — and God parted the sea and swallowed the enemy.

"You saw with your own eyes what I did." This was not a story they had merely heard; it was deliverance they had witnessed. God wanted them to remember that when they were utterly powerless, He acted powerfully on their behalf.

We have a greater exodus to remember. We too were once trapped — enslaved not to Pharaoh but to sin, with no power to free ourselves. And when we were helpless, God acted. He sent not Moses but His own Son, and through the cross He brought us out of bondage into freedom (Rom 6:17-18).

The wilderness came after the rescue, and God led them through that too. Perhaps you are in a wilderness season now, long after your rescue. Take heart. The God who brought you out will also bring you through. Remember with your own eyes what He has done, and trust Him for the road ahead.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Can you recall times God rescued you when you were helpless?
2. How does the exodus point you to your greater rescue in Christ?
3. If you are in a wilderness season, how does God's past faithfulness help?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Mighty God, thank You for bringing me out of slavery to sin through Christ. When I walk through wilderness seasons, help me trust the God who rescues to carry me through. Amen.
